主要内容: Behind China’s food scare: a US-owned meat plant. Chinese manufacturers may have a worrying track record with product safety, but it seems a U.S.-owned meat processing plant is at the center of the latest scandal to rock the country's fast-food sector. Shanghai Husi Food, the company under fire for reportedly supplying expired meat products to major restaurant chains including McDonald's, Yum Brands' KFC and Pizza Hut, is owned by Illinois-based OSI Group, one of the world's largest privately-held food processing companies. This case highlights how important it is for companies to have a very firm grasp of what is going on in their global operations. OSI Group, which first entered China in 1991, operates eight processing plants in mainland China and is the country's largest meat supplier. The scandal unfolded over the weekend when a report from Shanghai TV accused OSI Group's China affiliate of using expired meat and unhygienic practices. Authorities in Shanghai subsequently ordered the suspension of operations at Shanghai Husi. OSI Group issued a statement saying it was "appalled" by the revelations and has formed an investigation team to conduct its own internal review.
